properties.name: Cancun Hotel Zone
properties.verdict: Easiest first-time beachfront base — shortest ride from CUN
properties.description: A 22 km barrier-island resort strip along Boulevard Kukulcan between the Caribbean Sea and Nichupte Lagoon, lined with large all-inclusive hotels, beach clubs, and R1/R2 public buses.
properties.bestFor: First Cancun trip, short airport transfer, beachfront resorts with dining and tours at your doorstep.
properties.watchOut: Beach width and wave strength vary sharply by kilometer marker (north-facing Punta Cancun is calmest; east-facing blocks have stronger surf and occasional summer sargassum).
properties.logistics: Pre-booked shared/private transfers from CUN take 20–30 min. Within the Hotel Zone, frequent R1 and R2 buses run along Boulevard Kukulcan day and night (~12 MXN), avoiding expensive hotel-zone taxi fares.
properties.seasonsNote: Best weather: Dec–Apr (dry, warm, low humidity). May–Oct is hotter and carries sargassum and rain risk; north-facing beaches near Playa Mujeres / Punta Cancun stay noticeably clearer.

properties.name: Downtown Cancun (El Centro)
properties.verdict: Real Mexican food & budget stays — but no direct beach
properties.description: Mainland urban center of Cancun around Avenida Tulum, Parque Las Palapas, and the main ADO bus terminal — offering local prices, street food, and easy connections to Riviera Maya and islands.
properties.bestFor: Budget-conscious travelers, street-food fans, overnight layovers before ferries to Isla Mujeres or Holbox, and travelers using ADO buses.
properties.watchOut: There is no beachfront in Downtown Cancun — reaching public beaches in the Hotel Zone takes a 15–25 min bus or rideshare each way.
properties.logistics: ADO airport buses arrive directly at the Downtown terminal every 20–30 min. From here, R1/R2 city buses reach Hotel Zone beaches and Puerto Juarez ferries to Isla Mujeres.
properties.seasonsNote: Urban dining and day-trip hubs work year-round; summer humidity is more noticeable inland without sea breeze, making air-conditioned hotels worthwhile.

properties.name: Cancun International Airport (CUN)
properties.verdict: Main air gateway for Cancun, Riviera Maya, Tulum & islands
properties.description: Busiest international tourist airport in Mexico (Terminals 2, 3, and 4), sitting right off Highway 307 with direct ADO coaches and private transfers along the entire Caribbean coast.
properties.bestFor: Almost all international arrivals to Cancun, Playa del Carmen, Cozumel, Isla Mujeres, Puerto Morelos, Akumal, and Tulum.
properties.watchOut: Walk past the indoor timeshare/taxi hall ('shark tank') straight outside to your pre-booked transfer or official ADO booth; on-site airport taxis charge much higher rates.
properties.logistics: ADO coaches run from outside every terminal to Downtown Cancun, Playa del Carmen, and Tulum. Private vans are fastest for resorts along Highway 307 and groups of 2+.

properties.name: Isla Mujeres
properties.verdict: Calm-water island 20 min by ferry from Cancun
properties.description: A narrow 7 km Caribbean island directly across Bahia de Mujeres from Cancun, famous for shallow turquoise Playa Norte, golf-cart exploration, and laid-back sunsets.
properties.bestFor: Travelers seeking calm, wave-free swimming water, small boutique hotels, and a slower pace close to Cancun.
properties.watchOut: Last ferries limit evening flexibility if you stay on the mainland; staying on the island makes mainland day trips (chichen itza / cenotes) inconvenient.
properties.logistics: Ultramar ferries depart every 30 min from Puerto Juarez (plus select Hotel Zone piers like Playa Tortugas/El Embarcadero). Once on the island, Centro and Playa Norte are walkable; golf carts cover Punta Sur.
properties.seasonsNote: Playa Norte faces north-west, so it stays calmer and far more sheltered from sargassum than open east-facing Riviera Maya beaches.

properties.name: Isla Holbox
properties.verdict: Car-free sandbar island for bohemian stays & whale sharks
properties.description: A relaxed, sandy-street island north of the Yucatan Peninsula inside the Yum Balam reserve — far more remote than Isla Mujeres, known for shallow sandbars, sunsets, and summer whale shark tours.
properties.bestFor: Slow travel, boutique barefoot stays, bioluminescence/whale shark season, and disconnecting from mega-resorts.
properties.watchOut: Too far from CUN for a rushed day trip; sandy unpaved streets puddle heavily after rain, and mosquitoes can be intense around mangroves at dusk.
properties.logistics: Take a private transfer, rental car (leave parked in Chiquila), or ADO bus to Chiquila port (~2 hours from Cancun), then a 25-minute passenger ferry across the lagoon.
properties.seasonsNote: Dry season (Dec–Apr) gives the driest streets and clearest skies. Whale shark swimming season runs roughly June through mid-September.

properties.name: Puerto Morelos
properties.verdict: Quiet reef-side fishing town 25 min south of CUN
properties.description: A peaceful coastal town tucked between Cancun and Playa del Carmen, featuring a protected national marine reef right offshore and the Ruta de los Cenotes running inland.
properties.bestFor: Couples and families who want a calm, walkable beach town near CUN with easy snorkeling and Ruta de los Cenotes access without Cancun or Playa crowds.
properties.watchOut: Limited nightlife and shopping compared to Playa del Carmen; many large Riviera Maya resorts north/south of town sit far from the village center on Highway 307.
properties.logistics: Quick 25–35 min private transfer from CUN. Playa Express colectivos and ADO buses stop on Highway 307 (a short taxi ride from the beachside town center).
properties.seasonsNote: Protected offshore reef dampens big surf year-round, though summer sargassum can collect along parts of the coast.

properties.name: Playa del Carmen
properties.verdict: Most walkable Riviera Maya hub + Cozumel ferry pier
properties.description: Vibrant mid-coast city centered on pedestrian Quinta Avenida (5th Avenue), combining independent restaurants, city-center hotels, Playacar resorts, and direct ferries to Cozumel.
properties.bestFor: Travelers who want restaurants and nightlife on foot, easy ADO/colectivo day trips, or frequent ferry crossings to Cozumel.
properties.watchOut: Central beaches near the ferry pier are narrower and busier; staying right next to 12th Street clubs brings late-night noise.
properties.logistics: Direct ADO buses from CUN arrive right at 5th Avenue. Colectivos along Highway 307 connect south to Akumal and Tulum in 30–60 min; ferries to Cozumel depart every 30–60 min.
properties.seasonsNote: Central location makes it practical all year; Playacar (south end) and northern beaches offer more space during peak winter months.

properties.name: Cozumel
properties.verdict: World-class drift diving island off Playa del Carmen
properties.description: Mexico's largest Caribbean island, separated from Playa del Carmen by a 45-minute ferry channel and home to protected Mesoamerican reef walls, dive resorts, and a rugged eastern coast.
properties.bestFor: Scuba divers, snorkelers, and travelers wanting a relaxed island extension away from mainland Riviera Maya traffic.
properties.watchOut: Most western shores are rocky/ironshore rather than wide powdery sand (better for entering reef water than long beach walks); cruise ships bring midday crowds to San Miguel.
properties.logistics: Passenger ferries (Winjet/Ultramar/Xcaret) cross from Playa del Carmen pier in ~45 min; car ferries run from Calica. Cozumel also has its own airport (CZM).
properties.seasonsNote: West-facing reefs stay calm and clear for diving most of the year and largely avoid heavy sargassum buildup compared to the mainland.

properties.name: Akumal
properties.verdict: Calm bays for sea-turtle snorkeling between Playa & Tulum
properties.description: Protected coastal bay community along southern Riviera Maya famous for wild green sea turtles grazing in shallow seagrass, Yal-Ku Lagoon, and beachfront family & adults-only resorts.
properties.bestFor: Snorkeling with sea turtles, calmer bay swimming, and quieter all-inclusive resorts mid-way to Tulum.
properties.watchOut: Strict turtle-zone rules require a certified guide and life vest in protected sections; outside the resorts there is very little town nightlife.
properties.logistics: Reached in ~75 min south from CUN or ~55–65 min north from Tulum Airport (TQO) via Highway 307, plus frequent colectivos running between Playa del Carmen and Tulum.
properties.seasonsNote: Morning hours offer the calmest visibility in Akumal Bay; Half Moon Bay and Yal-Ku Lagoon provide sheltered snorkeling alternatives.

properties.name: Tulum
properties.verdict: Boutique beach clubs, Mayan ruins & cenotes — split town vs beach
properties.description: Southern Riviera Maya hotspot split into three distinct zones — inland Tulum Pueblo, residential Aldea Zama, and the narrow beachfront Hotel Zone — surrounded by cenotes and cliffside ruins.
properties.bestFor: Design-focused boutique trips, cenote hopping, ruins (Tulum & Coba), and beach-club aesthetics.
properties.watchOut: Long transfer from CUN (90–130 min); taxis between Tulum Pueblo and the Beach Zone are steep, and the single two-lane beach road often jams in high season.
properties.logistics: New Tulum Airport (TQO) cuts arrival drives (~35–45 min to Town, ~45–65 min to Beach Zone) compared to CUN. ADO buses connect both TQO and CUN to Tulum Centro; bikes work well inside Aldea Zama and Pueblo.
properties.seasonsNote: Nov–Apr offers the best beach conditions. May–Sep sees higher humidity and significant sargassum risk along Tulum's open beachfront, though freshwater cenotes remain clear year-round.

properties.name: Tulum International Airport (TQO)
properties.verdict: Southern Riviera Maya air gateway cutting Tulum & Akumal drive times
properties.description: Felipe Carrillo Puerto International Airport (TQO), opened in late 2023 in the jungle ~20 km southwest of Tulum Pueblo — a modern southern alternative to CUN for Tulum, Akumal, and southern Riviera Maya stays.
properties.bestFor: Travelers staying in Tulum (Pueblo, Aldea Zama, or Beach Zone) or Akumal who want to skip the 90–130 min Highway 307 drive from Cancun (CUN).
properties.watchOut: TQO sits ~20 km inland in the jungle, not next to the coast — reaching Tulum Beach Zone still takes 45–65 min, and walk-up airport taxis charge high fixed rates unless you pre-book a transfer or take ADO.
properties.logistics: ADO coaches connect TQO directly to Tulum Centro terminal. For beachfront hotels along the Tulum Hotel Zone or resorts in Akumal, pre-booked private vans or terminal rental cars are the smoothest choice.

properties.name: Punta Cana & Bavaro
properties.verdict: Dominican Republic's main eastern all-inclusive coastline
properties.description: Flagship eastern resort corridor stretching from Cap Cana through Bavaro to Uvero Alto. Detailed zone-by-zone guides are available in the Dominican Republic Hub.

properties.name: Punta Cana International Airport (PUJ)
properties.verdict: Primary tourist air hub for eastern Dominican Republic
properties.description: Busiest leisure gateway in the Dominican Republic, linked by Autopista del Coral to Cap Cana, Bavaro, Bayahibe, and La Romana.

properties.name: Bayahibe
properties.verdict: Calm Caribbean-side beach town & Saona Island departure port
properties.description: Caribbean-facing coastal base west of Punta Cana, positioned along calmer water with boat departures to Saona Island.

properties.name: Puerto Plata & North Coast
properties.verdict: Atlantic north coast for Cabarete surfing, Sosua & mountain views
properties.description: Northern Dominican coast linking Puerto Plata, Sosua, and kitesurfing hub Cabarete with direct POP airport access.

properties.name: Samana Peninsula
properties.verdict: Lush northeastern peninsula for nature & winter whale watching
properties.description: Mountainous northeastern peninsula around Las Terrenas and Samana Bay, known for coves, waterfalls, and winter humpback whales.

properties.name: Santo Domingo
properties.verdict: Historic capital city & Zona Colonial on the Caribbean coast
properties.description: Capital of the Dominican Republic featuring the UNESCO-listed Zona Colonial and highway links east toward La Romana and Punta Cana.

properties.name: Nassau (The Bahamas)
properties.verdict: Quick-flight Bahamas hub on New Providence & Paradise Island
properties.description: Capital island hub in The Bahamas, linked by bridge to Paradise Island and connected by short flights from the US East Coast.

properties.name: Providenciales (Turks & Caicos)
properties.verdict: Clear shallow turquoise reefs & Grace Bay beachfront
properties.description: Main tourism island of Turks and Caicos, anchored by Grace Bay Beach and shallow reef waters.

properties.name: Montego Bay (Jamaica)
properties.verdict: Jamaica's main northern resort coast & MBJ air gateway
properties.description: Northern resort hub of Jamaica along Highway A1, providing fast transfers from MBJ to beachfront resorts and excursions.

properties.name: San Juan (Puerto Rico)
properties.verdict: Historic Old San Juan & major Eastern Caribbean flight hub
properties.description: Primary gateway of Puerto Rico combining colonial Old San Juan, urban beach districts, and highway access to El Yunque.

properties.name: Aruba
properties.verdict: Dry sunny island outside the main Caribbean hurricane belt
properties.description: Southern Caribbean island favored for dry trade-wind weather outside the primary summer hurricane track.
